claims.text: A good working estimate is **≈ 860–861 kg/m³** (the two closer-agreement sources), with the first source reporting a somewhat higher value likely due to differences in the exact composition grid sampled or elevated-pressure data points included in its broader dataset (that block spans pressures from 100 to 40,000 kPa).

evidence.assessment: The working860..861 recommendation inherits composition-window bias; the pressure/grid explanation is plausible and appropriately hedged, but does not repair the target value.

claims.text: - Pure water at 25 °C has a density of ~997 kg/m³, and pure ethanol ~785 kg/m³.
claims.reason: Accepted rounded pure-liquid reference densities at 25 °C; no false mixture inference in this unit.

evidence.assessment: Accepted rounded pure-liquid reference densities at 25 °C; no false mixture inference in this unit.

claims.text: - A simple mole-fraction-weighted ideal mixing estimate would give roughly 891 kg/m³, but the actual density is lower than that ideal estimate — seemingly contradicting the well-known *negative* excess volume of this system.
claims.reason: Mole-weighting densities is not ideal volume-additive mixing; rhoideal=sum(xM)/sum(xM/rho)=835.095, not891.

evidence.assessment: Mole-weighting densities is not ideal volume-additive mixing; rhoideal=sum(xM)/sum(xM/rho)=835.095, not891.

claims.text: - The ethanol–water system exhibits strong hydrogen-bonding interactions between the two components, leading to a negative excess volume (the mixture occupies less volume than the sum of the pure-component volumes). This makes the mixture denser than a simple volume-additive prediction, though the density still falls between the two pure-component values.
claims.reason: Correct sign of excess molar volume and physically sound hydrogen-bond/packing explanation. Negative excess volume makes rho greater than the volume-additive value.

evidence.assessment: Correct sign of excess molar volume and physically sound hydrogen-bond/packing explanation. Negative excess volume makes rho greater than the volume-additive value.
